# Jeremiah 45 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The-word which Jeremiah the-prophet spoke to Baruch son-of Neriah, when-he-wrote these words in-a-scroll from-the-mouth-of Jeremiah, in-the-fourth year of-Jehoiakim son-of Josiah king-of Judah, saying:

**2** "Thus says YHWH God-of Israel to-you, Baruch:

**3** You-said, 'Woe now to-me, for YHWH has-added sorrow to-my-pain! I-am-weary with-my-groaning and-rest I-have-not-found.'"

**4** "Thus you-shall-say to-him, 'Thus says YHWH: Behold, what I-have-built I-am-tearing-down, and-what I-have-planted I-am-uprooting — and-all-this land.

**5** And-you, do-you-seek great-things for-yourself? Do-not-seek. For behold-Me bringing evil upon all flesh,' declares YHWH, 'but-I-will-give to-you your-life as-plunder in-all places where you go.'"

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **45:1**: Chronologically set in Jehoiakim's fourth year (605 BCE) — the same year as the battle of Carchemish. Baruch's personal crisis coincides with world-historical upheaval.

- **45:3**: Yaga'ti be-anachati — 'I am weary with my groaning.' Baruch's complaint mirrors Jeremiah's own laments, showing how prophetic ministry burdens those who serve alongside the prophet.

- **45:5**: Nafshekha lekha le-shalal — 'your life as plunder.' In a world being destroyed, survival itself is the prize. The language of military plunder applied to mere existence.

— EMET
